_doc: Five more episodic universes — The Orville, Stargate, Babylon 5, Firefly and Battlestar Galactica. All formats built to visit somewhere new each week, which is precisely the supply problem this catalogue had.

destinations.name: Moclus
destinations.blurb: A single-sex industrial world and the Union's main weapons supplier, run on discipline, forges and an official position on gender that the rest of the galaxy finds increasingly hard to sit next to.

destinations.name: Xelaya
destinations.blurb: A beautiful, cultured world with gravity so high its people are superhumanly strong anywhere else and increasingly fragile at home. Excellent architecture, exceptional universities, take the lift.

destinations.name: Sargus 4
destinations.blurb: A world like early-21st-century Earth, except justice is decided by public vote. Get enough down-votes and you are corrected. Be pleasant to everyone; the badge on their lapel is counting.

destinations.name: Kaylon 1
destinations.blurb: A machine world of immaculate order, built on the mass graves of the organic species that made it. Spotless, silent, and constantly evaluating whether your existence is justified.

destinations.name: Dorahl
destinations.blurb: A generation ship so vast its people forgot it was a ship, worshipping the reactor as a sun and treating the idea of an outside as heresy. The hull hatch is up a mountain, if you fancy it.

destinations.name: Regor 2
destinations.blurb: A contested colony world on the Krill border, notable for a nocturnal population who cannot survive daylight and a landscape that is nothing but daylight. Nights are lively.

destinations.name: Abydos
destinations.blurb: The first world through the Stargate: a desert of pyramids and naquadah mines, whose people were taken from Egypt thousands of years ago and taught to worship the being who took them.

destinations.name: Chulak
destinations.blurb: Forested world of the Jaffa, warrior-servants who carry a larval god in their belly in exchange for perfect health. A stern, honourable, tattooed culture, currently reconsidering the arrangement.

destinations.name: Atlantis, Lantea
destinations.blurb: The Ancients' city-ship, floating on an empty ocean in another galaxy — spires of glass and alloy, ten thousand years abandoned, and a very long way from anyone who could come and help.

destinations.name: Dakara
destinations.blurb: The sacred world where the Jaffa believe their species began, a plain of weathered temples above a device the Ancients left behind that can rewrite all life in a galaxy. Handle carefully.

destinations.name: Babylon 5
destinations.blurb: Five miles of rotating steel in neutral space, built so five species could argue instead of shoot. A quarter of a million residents, a garden in the middle, and a downbelow you should avoid.

destinations.name: Minbar
destinations.blurb: A cold world of crystal cities that sing when the wind crosses them, run by a caste system of workers, warriors and religious, none of whom will give you a straight answer about anything.

destinations.name: Centauri Prime
destinations.blurb: A faded empire that still throws the best parties in the galaxy — opera, palace intrigue, exceptional drink, and a court where every compliment is a manoeuvre and the hair indicates rank.

destinations.name: Narn
destinations.blurb: A world stripped to bedrock by a century of Centauri occupation, rebuilt by a people who remember every day of it. Harsh, proud, deeply religious, and not remotely interested in forgiving.

destinations.name: Z'ha'dum
destinations.blurb: A dead world with a very old city buried underneath it, home to something that has been arranging galactic wars for its own reasons for a million years. People who go there do not come back.

destinations.name: Persephone
destinations.blurb: A border world of grand estates and open-air docks, where the wealthy hold masked balls uphill and everyone else works the shipyards downhill. Good place to pick up work you shouldn't take.

destinations.name: Whitefall
destinations.blurb: A fourth moon of Athens with maybe two thousand settlers, one crime boss called Patience, and a great deal of open grass. She has shot a visitor before. She will probably do it again.

destinations.name: Miranda
destinations.blurb: A terraformed world of thirty million, left off every star chart. The cities are intact, the power still runs, and everyone lay down and stopped. Something in the air made them stop.

destinations.name: Caprica
destinations.blurb: The wealthiest of the Twelve Colonies — beaches, universities, glass towers and a pyramid league — photographed here on a good day, shortly before it stopped being habitable.

destinations.name: Kobol
destinations.blurb: The world all twelve colonies came from, abandoned two thousand years ago and left to the forest — an opera house in ruins, a tomb full of stars, and scripture that turns out to be directions.

destinations.name: New Caprica
destinations.blurb: A cold, marginal world hidden inside a nebula, settled by a fleet that could not keep running. Tent city, thin soil, one year of hard-won ordinary life, and then the ships came back.
